about: The host that builds the project's reference tables from their publishers' releases, the builders it runs, and the feed an app reads them from.
capabilities: Checking a feed against its shapes · Shapes.read(), shapes.violations(), feedViolations()
Recording when each source was last checked · checked.json, mergeChecked()
Reading a release's files · csv(), delimited(), fixedWidth(), jsonLines(), xlsx(), xmlElements()
Checking that a builder conforms · conformanceExamples(), runConformance()
Vaccine codes and groups from CDC's CVX files · builders/cdc-cvx
ICD-10-CM code conversions from CDC's files · builders/cdc-icd-10-cm
Drug codes from NLM's prescribable RxNorm · builders/nlm-rxnorm-prescribable
Drug classes from VA's MED-RT · builders/va-med-rt
Lab codes and panels from Regenstrief's LOINC · builders/regenstrief-loinc
Variant classifications from NCBI's ClinVar · builders/ncbi-clinvar
Building a version of a table · build(), Feed.rowsOf()
Carrying forward the rows of a code that leaves a release · carry(), withProperty()
Describing what a version changed · differences(), differenceLines(), markdown()
Downloading a publisher's file patiently · patientFetch()
Finding a rows file in GitHub releases · releaseStore()
Running the host from the command line · host/src/cli.ts
Rules a host follows, run on this host · rules/steps.md
build: The published feed, held to its shapes · feed/feed.ttl
The licences the source shape lists, held to vocab/licences.ttl

glossary.definition: a public page on which a publisher names its versions; a source detected by its announcement is never downloaded by the host.
here, the code that turns one publisher's release into rows: a `build.ts` beside the `source.ttl` that declares its source. It touches no network and no file it was not handed.
of a mapping row, how many codes map to how many: `1:1`, `1:n` (one code became several) or `n:1` (several became one).
to keep, in a new version, the rows of a code the publisher's release no longer names.
in ICD-10-CM's conversions, a code replaced by a code that was itself replaced later; the builder follows it to the codes in effect.
here, a host asking a publisher whether it has a release newer than the feed's current versions.
ClinVar's statement of what a variant means for health, such as pathogenic or benign.
the public archive, kept by the US National Library of Medicine, of how laboratories classify variants, from benign to pathogenic; one of the reference tables.
a published list of codes for one kind of thing, such as RxNorm for medicines, LOINC for lab tests and SNOMED CT for clinical findings.
in ICD-10-CM, CDC's statement that a code of a new year takes the place of earlier ones.
the RDF a source is declared in (`source.ttl`, `builder.ttl`).
the rows a version added, removed and changed against the version it revises.
a group of medicines that work alike or are built alike, such as ACE inhibitors, as the US Food and Drug Administration assigns them.
established pharmacologic class: FDA's name for the drug class on a medicine's label.
a variant written in HGVS, the standard notation, such as `NM_000249.4:c.2042C>T`; a record's expression finds its row.
a plain-text file that states rules, each with examples written as steps (given, when, then); this repository's are under `rules/`.
a published list of the versions of reference tables, which an app reads to find newer ones.
here, something a builder left out of its rows and says so, such as a term it cannot map; it is shown with the differences and does not stop the build.
what RxNav, NLM's lookup service, says became of one code: still active, or retired and replaced by which.
here, the program that runs builders: it detects a release, downloads it, checks the rows, names the version and publishes. This repository's `host/` is one.
of a series, its name as a person reads it, such as 'Vaccine groups'; a feed gives it and a check updates it.
a row saying one code relates to another by a property, such as "is a member of".
a row giving a code its name.
the US National Library of Medicine, which publishes RxNorm and the history of its codes.
a set of lab tests reported together, such as a thyroid panel.
a particular form of an ingredient, such as lisinopril anhydrous of lisinopril, which some medicine products are tied to.
of a drug, that a clinician can prescribe as it is named; NLM publishes the RxNorm subset of such drugs as its prescribable content.
the organisation that issues a code system's releases, such as CDC, NLM or Regenstrief.
on GitHub, a proposed change that a person reads and accepts or rejects.
an HTTP request for a file from a given byte on, which a server answers with only the rest of the file.
the error thrown when the package declines a request it understood, such as a name it does not have; it has written nothing.
the Regenstrief Institute, which publishes LOINC.
one issue of a publisher's files, such as RxNorm's of a given month. (A "GitHub release" is always written so.)
the short text a check gives a release to tell it from the others: its Last-Modified date or its release version; `unlabelled` when the publisher gives neither.
ClinVar's statement of how well a classification is supported, such as `criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts`.
of a version, to take the place of its series' current version.
one line of a table: of a view, what one view entry holds, a cell per column; of a reference table, what it says of one code or variant.
the file holding one version's rows: gzipped N-Quads, named by its checksum.
one of the reference tables across its versions, such as RxNorm's product ingredients.
requirements on what a feed or a source's declaration must state, written in SHACL, the W3C language for checking data; each has a message saying what is wrong.
here, one publisher's release as a host is told of it in `source.ttl`: where it is, how a new one is detected, its files, its licence and the series it fills.
a row saying a code is retired, and which codes replace it.
a laboratory that sent ClinVar its classification of a variant.
what a reference table's rows say, such as product ingredients or vaccine groups; the vocabulary declares each kind.
RxNorm's kind of a concept: `IN` an ingredient, `PIN` a precise ingredient, `SCD`, `SBD`, `GPCK`, `BPCK` kinds of product.
one statement of RDF, made of a subject, a property and a value.
of text, that cannot be read as the kind of thing it should be, such as a date that is no date.
a difference in one of a person's genes from the reference sequence, as a genetic test reports it.
ClinVar's record of one variant, with a number such as 90011.
in the vocabulary's tests, an input written down beside the output every implementation must give for it.
here, one series' rows as built from one release; it is named by its content and never changed once published.
one way a feed or a declaration breaks a shape, as text ending in the shape's message.
